title: Daniel Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Daniel chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Daniel Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Daniel Chapter 9.

questions.question: In the first year of whose reign did Daniel understand the number of years mentioned by the LORD to Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:1 states that it was in the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus that Daniel understood the years.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9, how many years did the LORD say would accomplish the desolations of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:2 mentions that the word of the LORD to Jeremiah was that seventy years would accomplish the desolations of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did Daniel use as a sign of his humility and earnestness when praying to the LORD?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:3 states that Daniel sought God by prayer and supplications with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

questions.question: In Daniel's prayer, how does he describe God?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:4 describes God as the great and dreadful God, keeping covenant and mercy.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9, what have the people done that caused their current state?
options: Sinned and rebelled by departing from God's precepts
questions.correctAnswer: Sinned and rebelled by departing from God's precepts
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:5 states they have sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled by departing from God's precepts.

questions.question: Who does Daniel say the people have not listened to, according to Daniel 9?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:6 says they have not hearkened unto God's servants the prophets who spoke in His name.

questions.question: To whom does Daniel attribute righteousness in his prayer?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:7 states that righteousness belongs to the Lord.

questions.question: Who does Daniel say experiences confusion of face because of sin?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:8 says confusion of face belongs to kings, princes, and fathers because of sin.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9, what belongs to the Lord our God despite rebellion?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:9 states that mercies and forgiveness belong to the Lord though there has been rebellion.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel prayed to the LORD with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes to seek Him.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:3 confirms Daniel sought the LORD with prayer, supplications, fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

questions.question: True or False: According to Daniel 9, the people had obeyed the voice of the LORD and walked in His laws.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:10 states they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD to walk in His laws.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel confesses that all Israel have transgressed the law and that curses have been poured upon them.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:11 confirms that all Israel transgressed the law and curses have come upon them.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel says the evil upon Jerusalem has never been done before under the whole heaven.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:12 states that under the whole heaven nothing like the evil upon Jerusalem has been done.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first action Daniel took in his prayer according to Daniel 9?
options: Set his face unto the LORD God
questions.correctAnswer: Set his face unto the LORD God
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:3 shows the first action was setting his face unto the LORD God to seek Him.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9, what is the reason given for Jerusalem and the people becoming a reproach to those around them?
options: Because of their sins and iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: Because of their sins and iniquities
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:16 states that Jerusalem and the people became a reproach because of their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

medium.title: Daniel Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Daniel Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:10, what have the people failed to do in relation to God's voice?
options: They have obeyed the voice of the LORD
They have not obeyed the voice of the LORD
They have ignored the prophets but obeyed the law
They have followed the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: They have not obeyed the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:10 explicitly states that the people have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God, failing to walk in His laws given by the prophets, highlighting disobedience and rebellion.

questions.question: What consequence does Daniel 9:11 say has come upon Israel because they transgressed the law?
options: The curse and the oath written in the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The curse and the oath written in the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:11 explains that all Israel transgressed the law and did not obey, resulting in the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses coming upon them as punishment for their sins.

questions.question: What does Daniel 9:12 reveal about the nature of the evil brought upon Jerusalem?
options: It was a small and common trouble
It was a great evil never done under the whole heaven
It was a blessing in disguise
It was caused by neighboring nations only
questions.correctAnswer: It was a great evil never done under the whole heaven
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:12 states that the evil brought upon Jerusalem was confirmed by God's words and was a great evil unparalleled under the whole heaven, emphasizing the severity of Jerusalem's punishment.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:13, what had the people failed to do that might have changed their situation?
options: They failed to build the temple
They failed to make prayer before the LORD to turn from iniquities and understand truth
They failed to obey the king
They failed to fast and wear sackcloth
questions.correctAnswer: They failed to make prayer before the LORD to turn from iniquities and understand truth
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:13 shows that though the evil was written in the law, the people had not prayed to the LORD to turn from their sins and understand His truth, which could have altered their fate.

questions.question: What reason does Daniel 9:14 give for the LORD bringing evil upon the people?
options: Because the people obeyed His voice
Because the people disobeyed His voice and the LORD is righteous in all His works
questions.correctAnswer: Because the people disobeyed His voice and the LORD is righteous in all His works
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:14 explains that the LORD brought evil upon them because they disobeyed His voice, and emphasizes God's righteousness in all His actions, showing divine justice.

questions.question: How does Daniel 9:15 remind the LORD of His past deeds on behalf of His people?
options: By mentioning their victories over enemies
By recalling how He brought His people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and gained renown
By describing the building of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: By recalling how He brought His people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and gained renown
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:15 appeals to God's past deliverance of Israel from Egypt with great power and His renown, invoking His faithfulness despite their current sinfulness.

questions.question: What is Daniel's request in Daniel 9:16 regarding Jerusalem and God's wrath?
options: That God's anger remain upon Jerusalem
That God's anger and fury be turned away from Jerusalem because of their sins and the reproach it has become
That Jerusalem be given to foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: That God's anger and fury be turned away from Jerusalem because of their sins and the reproach it has become
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:16 petitions God to turn away His anger and fury from Jerusalem, acknowledging their sins and the reproach Jerusalem and its people have become to surrounding nations.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:17, what does Daniel ask God to do for His desolate sanctuary?
options: To cause His face to shine upon it for the Lord's sake
To give it to another nation
questions.correctAnswer: To cause His face to shine upon it for the Lord's sake
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:17 asks God to hear the prayers and cause His face to shine upon the desolate sanctuary, showing a plea for restoration and favor for God's own name's sake.

questions.question: In Daniel 9:18, why do the people not present their supplications before God?
options: Not for their righteousness but for God's great mercies
questions.correctAnswer: Not for their righteousness but for God's great mercies
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:18 clarifies that their prayers are not based on their righteousness, but they appeal to God's great mercies, showing humility and dependence on God's compassion.

questions.question: What does Daniel 9:19 urge God not to do for His own sake?
options: Delay in hearing, forgiving, and acting
questions.correctAnswer: Delay in hearing, forgiving, and acting
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:19 pleads with God not to defer His hearing, forgiveness, and action, emphasizing urgency for His own name's sake because the city and people bear His name.

questions.question: How does Daniel 9:11 help us understand the importance of obedience to God's law in practical living?
options: Disobedience causes curses and serious consequences
God's law was only for ancient times
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience causes curses and serious consequences
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:11 teaches that transgressing God's law leads to curses and punishment, underscoring the practical need for obedience to God's commands in daily life.

questions.question: What does Daniel 9:13 suggest will happen if the people had prayed and turned from their iniquities?
options: They might have been spared from evil and understood God's truth
questions.correctAnswer: They might have been spared from evil and understood God's truth
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:13 indicates that failure to pray and turn away from sin prevented the people from understanding God's truth and potentially avoiding the evil foretold in the law.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:14, how is the LORD described in relation to the works He does?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:14 affirms that the LORD is righteous in all His actions, emphasizing that the evil brought upon them was a just consequence of their disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Daniel 9:16, Jerusalem and its people are a reproach to those around them because of the sins of the current generation only.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:16 mentions that Jerusalem and its people are a reproach because of the sins and iniquities of the current generation and their fathers, showing that past and present sins contribute to their state.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel 9:19 urges God to hear, forgive, and act without delay for the sake of His city and people.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:19 explicitly calls on God not to delay in hearing, forgiving, or acting, because the city and people bear His name, demonstrating urgency in prayer and God's response.

hard.title: Daniel Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Daniel Chapter 9.

questions.question: What is Daniel specifically asking God to do for Jerusalem in Daniel 9:16?
options: Turn away His anger and fury
Send a new king to rule
questions.correctAnswer: Turn away His anger and fury
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:16 shows Daniel pleading with God to turn away His anger and fury from Jerusalem because of their sins and iniquities.

questions.question: Who comes to Daniel during his prayer to give him skill and understanding?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:21-22 records that the man Gabriel came swiftly to Daniel to give him skill and understanding during his prayer.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:24, what is one of the purposes of the 'seventy weeks' determined upon Daniel's people and city?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:24 states that the seventy weeks are determined to finish the transgression among other purposes like making an end of sins and bringing everlasting righteousness.

questions.question: In Daniel 9:25, how long after the commandment to restore Jerusalem will the Messiah come?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:25 specifies that from the commandment to restore Jerusalem unto the Messiah Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks (sixty-two weeks).

questions.question: What event does Daniel 9:26 say will happen after the sixty-two weeks?
options: The Messiah will be cut off
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah will be cut off
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:26 foretells that after sixty-two weeks, the Messiah will be cut off but not for Himself, indicating a sacrificial death.

questions.question: What will the prince who comes after the Messiah do according to Daniel 9:26?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:26 says the people of the prince that shall come will destroy the city and sanctuary, signaling a siege or destruction of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What happens in the midst of the 'one week' mentioned in Daniel 9:27?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:27 states that in the midst of that week he shall cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of 'seventy years' of desolation that Daniel references in Daniel 9:2?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:2 references the seventy years of desolations of Jerusalem as prophesied by Jeremiah, which is found in Jeremiah 25:11-12.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Daniel 9:24 to convey multiple purposes of the seventy weeks?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:24 uses parallelism by listing multiple related purposes of the seventy weeks in a balanced and poetic structure.

questions.question: What Hebrew meaning of the word 'Messiah' as used in Daniel 9:25 can be understood?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Messiah' (מָשִׁיחַ, Mashiach) means 'Anointed One', indicating one set apart by God for a special purpose, as used in Daniel 9:25.

questions.question: According to Daniel 9:19, for whose sake should God not defer in hearing and forgiving?
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:19 implores God not to defer for His own sake, emphasizing God's reputation and covenant name connected to His city and people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with Daniel 9:26's prophecy about the Messiah being cut off?
questions.explanation: John 19:30, describing Jesus' death on the cross, connects with Daniel 9:26's prophecy about the Messiah being cut off, not for Himself but for others.

questions.question: What theme from Daniel 9 is fulfilled in the New Testament book of Hebrews, especially regarding reconciliation and everlasting righteousness?
options: Jesus as the high priest making reconciliation
The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus as the high priest making reconciliation
questions.explanation: Hebrews explains Jesus as the high priest who makes reconciliation for iniquity and brings everlasting righteousness, fulfilling Daniel 9:24's themes.

questions.question: Daniel 9:20 mentions Daniel presenting his supplication before the LORD for what specific place?
options: The holy mountain of my God
questions.correctAnswer: The holy mountain of my God
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:20 notes Daniel presenting his supplication for the holy mountain of his God, referring to Jerusalem or Zion.

questions.question: True or False: Daniel 9:23 reveals that Gabriel came to Daniel because he was greatly beloved and to help him understand the vision.
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:23 explicitly says Gabriel came to Daniel because he was greatly beloved and to help him understand the vision.

theological.title: Daniel Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Daniel Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Daniel acknowledge in his prayer regarding the condition of Israel?
options: They have sinned and committed iniquity
They have turned away from their heritage
questions.correctAnswer: They have sinned and committed iniquity
questions.explanation: Daniel confesses, 'We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly' (Daniel 9:5). This acknowledges the sinful state of Israel before God.

questions.question: According to Daniel, what period did the Lord reveal through Jeremiah the prophet?
questions.explanation: Daniel understood from the books that the Lord would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem (Daniel 9:2).

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized when Daniel speaks of God's mercy?
questions.explanation: Daniel states, 'To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses' (Daniel 9:9), highlighting God's merciful nature.

questions.question: What does verse 14 indicate about the nature of God in relation to human behavior?
options: God is indifferent to human actions
God is righteous in all His works
questions.correctAnswer: God is righteous in all His works
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes God's righteousness: 'for the LORD our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth' (Daniel 9:14).

questions.question: What does Daniel request from God regarding Jerusalem in his prayer?
options: To turn away His anger and fury
questions.correctAnswer: To turn away His anger and fury
questions.explanation: Daniel beseeches God, 'let thine anger and thy fury be turned away from thy city Jerusalem' (Daniel 9:16).

questions.question: What does the term 'seventy weeks' in verse 24 signify in a theological context?
options: A timeframe for fulfilling God's plan of redemption
questions.correctAnswer: A timeframe for fulfilling God's plan of redemption
questions.explanation: The 'seventy weeks' are determined for significant events in God's redemptive plan, including reconciliation and bringing in everlasting righteousness (Daniel 9:24).

questions.question: Which aspect of God's character is revealed through Daniel's acknowledgment of Israel's transgressions?
questions.explanation: Daniel recognizes that despite their sins, 'To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses' (Daniel 9:9), showcasing God's forgiving nature.

questions.question: In what way does Daniel's prayer reflect the communal aspect of sin?
options: He only confesses his own sins
He includes the sins of his people
He ignores the issue of sin
questions.correctAnswer: He includes the sins of his people
questions.explanation: Daniel confesses, 'I prayed... confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel' (Daniel 9:20), reflecting a communal acknowledgment of sin.

questions.question: What significant event does verse 26 foreshadow regarding the Messiah?
options: The Messiah will be cut off
The Messiah will be a military leader
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah will be cut off
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself' (Daniel 9:26), indicating a prophetic foreshadowing of the Messiah's death.

questions.question: How does Daniel's prayer in verse 18 express humility before God?
questions.explanation: Daniel states, 'for we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies' (Daniel 9:18), showing humility and dependence on God's mercy.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 11-12 convey about the consequences of disobedience?
options: Disobedience leads to curses and disasters
The law of Moses is irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to curses and disasters
questions.explanation: Daniel states, 'therefore the curse is poured upon us... because we have sinned against him' (Daniel 9:11-12), illustrating the serious consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the city which is called by thy name' in verse 18 imply about Jerusalem's identity?
questions.explanation: Daniel refers to Jerusalem as 'the city which is called by thy name' (Daniel 9:18), indicating its special status as God's chosen city.

questions.question: What does the angel Gabriel's arrival signify about divine communication in verse 21?
options: God sends messengers to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God sends messengers to His people
questions.explanation: Gabriel's swift arrival signifies that God actively communicates and sends messengers to His people, as seen when he touched Daniel (Daniel 9:21).

questions.question: What theological understanding does the phrase 'to make an end of sins' convey in verse 24?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'to make an end of sins' indicates God's plan to ultimately eradicate sin through His redemptive work (Daniel 9:24).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the prophecies in Daniel are too vague to be meaningful. What do Daniel 9:24-27 actually teach about God's specific plans for redemption?
options: They provide a detailed timeline of redemption
They focus only on Israel's failures
They are irrelevant to salvation history
questions.correctAnswer: They provide a detailed timeline of redemption
questions.explanation: Daniel 9:24-27 outlines a specific timeline for events related to sin, reconciliation, and the coming of the Messiah, affirming God's detailed redemptive plan.
